Repo: C:\Users\felth\Downloads\FlowGuard (run all commands from the `server` subdirectory).

Context: `server/middlewares/auth.js` `verifyToken` was just changed to be DB-backed. After JWT verification it does `const { User } = require('../models')` and, when `User.findByPk` is a function, calls `await User.findByPk(decoded.id)`. It then requires: account exists (else 401), `account.isActive !== false` (else 403), and `Number(decoded.tokenVersion ?? 0) === Number(account.tokenVersion ?? 0)` (else 401). It sets `req.user = { id, email, role, tokenVersion }` FROM THE DB ROW — the DB role is authoritative, not the JWT role. If the mocked models export has no usable `User.findByPk`, it falls back to `req.user = decoded` (JWT-only). Note `verifyServiceOrRole` still short-circuits on a valid `x-service-key` header WITHOUT any DB lookup.

Task: make these three Jest suites pass again by adapting ONLY their mock arrangement to the new middleware:
1. server/tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/attendance-scan.test.js
2. server/tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/access-event.test.js
3. server/tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/facialRecognition.test.js

The typical failure: suites mock `../../models` with `User: { findByPk: jest.fn() }` which resolves `undefined` by default, so authenticated requests now die in the middleware with 401 "Account no longer exists", or the middleware consumes a `mockResolvedValueOnce` intended for the route.

Recommended pattern (already used successfully in server/tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/rbac.test.js and tests/user.test.js — read them for reference): give `User.findByPk` a default `mockImplementation` keyed by user id, set inside `beforeEach` AFTER `jest.clearAllMocks()` (clearAllMocks does not remove implementations, but re-setting it in beforeEach is safest since some tests override with mockResolvedValue). For each suite, look at the ids signed into the JWTs (e.g. `jwt.sign({ id: 1, role: "FM" }...)`) and make findByPk return `{ id, role, isActive: true }` matching those ids. Where a test overrides `findByPk` with `mockResolvedValue`/`mockResolvedValueOnce` for a ROUTE-level lookup (e.g. resolving the recognized user id 25), rewrite that override as an id-keyed `mockImplementation` so the middleware lookup (auth id) AND the route lookup (target id) both resolve correctly.

Hard rules:
- Do NOT modify anything under server/routes, server/middlewares, server/models, or any non-test file.
- Do NOT change expected status codes, expected messages, or weaken/delete assertions. The tests' intent must remain identical; only the mock plumbing may change. Adding a brief comment explaining the DB-backed auth mock is welcome.
- If a test asserts findByPk call counts/args, adjust thoughtfully (the middleware adds one extra findByPk call per authenticated request) — prefer `toHaveBeenCalledWith` over exact call counts.

Verify with: `npx jest "tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/attendance-scan.test.js" "tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/access-event.test.js" "tests/Tan Xiu Li, Felicia/facialRecognition.test.js"` — all must pass.

Return: a short summary of what you changed per file and the final jest output tail (suite/test counts).

All three suites pass. Only mock plumbing changed — no route/middleware/model files touched, no assertions or expected statuses altered.

## What changed per file

Each file got the same pattern (mirroring `rbac.test.js`): an id-keyed `AUTH_USERS` table (`1: FM`, `60: Staff`, both `isActive: true`, matching the ids signed into the JWTs) plus a `primeDb(extra)` helper that sets `mockUser.findByPk.mockImplementation((id) => Promise.resolve(table[id] ?? null))`. `primeDb()` is called in every `beforeEach` after `jest.clearAllMocks()`, so the DB-backed `verifyToken` always resolves the authenticated account.

1. **`C:\Users\felth\Downloads\FlowGuard\server\tests\Tan Xiu Li, Felicia\attendance-scan.test.js`** — added the helper; all three `beforeEach` blocks now prime the auth users; every route-level `mockUser.findByPk.mockResolvedValue(...)` override was rewritten as `primeDb({ 25: activeUser })` / `primeDb({ 25: { ...activeUser, isActive: false } })` / `primeDb({ 25: { ...activeUser, isEnrolled: false } })` / `primeDb({ 9999: null })`, so the middleware lookup (id 1/60) and the route lookup (id 25/9999) each resolve their own row. The blanket `mockResolvedValue(activeUser)` would otherwise have fed the Staff-role row (id 25) to the middleware for the FM token and produced a spurious 403.

2. **`C:\Users\felth\Downloads\FlowGuard\server\tests\Tan Xiu Li, Felicia\access-event.test.js`** — same helper; `beforeEach` primes auth users (kept `resetLogCooldowns()` and the `SecurityLog.create` default); the four `findByPk` overrides (active, dedup, suspended, unknown-404) converted to id-keyed `primeDb(...)` calls.

3. **`C:\Users\felth\Downloads\FlowGuard\server\tests\Tan Xiu Li, Felicia\facialRecognition.test.js`** — same helper; all three `beforeEach` blocks prime auth users; the three route-level overrides (recognised-FM user 25, suspended user 25, stale AI match 999 → null) converted to `primeDb(...)`. The `toHaveBeenCalledWith(25, expect.any(Object))` assertion still passes untouched since the route's call matches regardless of the middleware's extra `findByPk(1)` call.

No call-count assertions on `findByPk` existed, so none needed adjusting; `SecurityLog.create` count assertions are unaffected (the middleware writes no logs).
